key_insight: LLM serving decisions split into two distinct levers: hardware/configuration mainly drives energy, while deployment location and time can change carbon, water, and biodiversity impacts enough to alter the optimal choice.
engineering_relevance: For system operators, this means sustainability-aware routing and provisioning should optimize beyond energy alone, because the same serving setup can look very different across environmental metrics.
method: Unified framework (PRISM) to characterize LLM serving impacts across energy, carbon, water, and biodiversity.
Separates configuration effects from deployment effects and identifies when rankings stay invariant or diverge.
Quantifies cross-dimensional regret and balances all four sustainability dimensions.
evidence_signal: In regional-routing experiments, PRISM reduced median worst-case regret by 50.2% versus the strongest baseline.
watch_item: The framework’s conclusions depend on deployment-specific and lifecycle assumptions, so embodied-impact thresholds and regional data quality may affect real-world applicability.
paper_title: Beyond Energy: When Sustainability Dimensions Reshape LLM Serving Decisions
